## Why

From 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-20 the global git config had `user.name=test` / `user.email=test@test.com`, so every lane and agent commit was authored "test". Nothing flagged it. Operator request 2026-10-20: "should probably have a product check for this too".

## What

- `we:scripts/lib/git-identity.mjs`: a pure `checkGitIdentity({name, email})` returning ok / placeholder / missing. The placeholder list is a cascade setting (`gitIdentityPlaceholders`) that can only add to the built-in list. Each key accepts only a plain array of non-empty strings; anything else is ignored with a warning.
- **SessionStart bootstrap** (`we:scripts/bootstrap-session.mjs`): a new `git-identity` line. It shows `drift` on a placeholder or missing identity, so `--check` exits 1.
- **`lane-pool.mjs status` / `provision`**: warn when git resolves a placeholder author in a lane, and when a lane's effective `core.hooksPath` is not `.githooks`. Provision, refresh and acquire set `core.hooksPath` themselves (idempotent, logged), so the guard runs with `--no-install` and in `--reference` clones. `status` stays write-free.
- **Commit guard** (`.githooks/pre-commit` runs `we:scripts/guard-git-identity.mjs`): in lane clones it refuses a commit whose author or committer is a placeholder or missing, and prints how to fix it. Any unexpected error also refuses the commit (fail closed, per operator ruling). It works from paths with spaces or symlinks.

## Proof (live)

With a copy of the incident config (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` pointing at a `test`/`test@test.com` file):
- the guard exits 1 and refuses the commit;
- `bootstrap-session --check` prints `drift git-identity PLACEHOLDER …` and exits 1;
- `lane-pool status` prints `⚠ git identity PLACEHOLDER in 1 lane(s)`.

With the real identity, all three pass. 218 targeted tests pass through heavy admission, including real `git commit` runs through the hook, a provision with `--no-install`, a worktree-scope override, and a path with a space.

## Audit

5 Codex read-only audit rounds. The round-5 verdict, verbatim:

> - `scripts/lib/git-identity.mjs:74` — **High:** Malformed nested settings erase valid lower-layer additions: platform `extraNames: ["CI Service"]` plus tool `extraNames: {nested: []}` makes that placeholder pass; empty objects also escape the required warning.
> - `scripts/lib/git-identity.mjs:232` — **High:** Multiple local `core.hooksPath` values make repair fail silently because the error is returned without logging and callers discard it, allowing acquire to hand out a lane whose guards remain disabled.
> - `scripts/lib/git-identity.mjs:62` — **Medium:** Normal guard/bootstrap/lane-pool invocations emit no placeholder-setting source diagnostic because cascade logging defaults off outside daemons, violating the logged-source requirement.
> - `scripts/lane-pool.mjs:2841` — **Medium:** Human-readable `status --leased-only` probes unleased lanes again; the added reporting loop performed 300 synchronous git calls in 4.6 seconds for 100 entries, defeating the existing skip optimization.
>
> VERDICT: WEAKENED — malformed settings can remove configured protection, hook repair can fail silently, source logging is absent by default, and status regresses pool-scan performance.

**Operator acceptance (2026-10-20, "ok"):** stop iterating and open this PR. The 4 points above are filed as follow-up card `x89ywtw` (not queued), which this PR includes.

soak-waiver: new identity check plus a lane pre-commit guard; no daemon behaviour changes, so there is no daemon failure to replay (lane-pool only adds a status warning and an idempotent core.hooksPath set, covered by real-git tests).

### What changed
1. `ensureLaneHooksPath` (`scripts/lib/git-identity.mjs`) now runs a new injected `hookRunnable` check: readable + executable (the same `access(X_OK)` test git uses) + a regular file. If it fails, the result is `error` on both the read path and the write path. The tracked file is never chmod-ed, and `writeLaneEnv` refuses the lane.
2. Self-review variant: `existsSync` follows symlinks. A tracked pre-commit that was deleted, or replaced by a dangling symlink, used to come back as `skipped`, which is allow-listed. Now `skipped` is returned only when `git ls-files --error-unmatch` says the hook is untracked (exit 1). A tracked but missing hook is `error`, and so is any other git failure.
3. `lane-pool status` now uses the same allow-list as `writeLaneEnv` (`ok|set|skipped`). Before, it used a separate deny-list, so a new failure status could have passed as hooked. Its wording now covers the not-runnable case.
